sections.overview: Eucrostes indigenata is a Mediterranean geometrid moth recorded from Europe, North Africa and the eastern Mediterranean.
sections.identification: The French lepidopterist account places it in Geometridae, subfamily Geometrinae, but gives no standard body measurements.
sections.habitat: French records shown by Lepinet are concentrated along the Mediterranean coast; the broader records span the Mediterranean region.
sections.diet: Its caterpillars feed on spurges, plants of the genus Euphorbia.
sections.behavior: LepiWiki documents adults as well as immature stages, including observations of adults attracted to light.
sections.reproduction: The LepiWiki record includes eggs, caterpillars and pupae, but does not establish a complete seasonal breeding schedule.
sections.ecology: The recorded larval association with Euphorbia links its development to spurge plants within its Mediterranean range.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted document taxonomy and regional occurrence but provide no current global population trend or status assessment.
